claim.provenance_disclaimer: HYBRID PROVENANCE. The structured anchor record holds fields transcribed from real Chicago crash data supplied by the project owner. Every narrative document is SYNTHETIC and is not a statement by any real crash participant. No person-level demographic attribute is carried into this fixture. Results measured against it record WHAT WE PLANTED (D-003); the real anchor makes the scenario physically plausible, it does not make the evaluation real-world evidence.
claim.verified_means: Verified means this assertion was traced to exact text in a source document and that citation was checked in code. It does NOT mean the assertion is true. No stage of this system decides which source is correct, which differences matter, or anything about credibility, liability, or fraud.

ex_007.text: The claimant did not initially realize how significant the contact was.

evidence.quote: did not initially realize how significant the contact was
evidence.passage_text:
The claimant reports that their vehicle was traveling northbound on Karlov Avenue at night. The claimant says the road was wet and visibility was limited by darkness, although the roadway was illuminated.

The claimant reports that the vehicle was turning right when it came into contact with a parked vehicle. The claimant says they did not initially realize how significant the contact was.

The claimant states that they stopped briefly, looked at the vehicles, and then left because they were concerned about being stranded late at night. The claimant says they did not see anyone inside the parked vehicle and did not believe anyone was injured.

ex_022.text: The claimant did not believe anyone was injured.

evidence.quote: did not believe anyone was injured
evidence.passage_text:
The claimant says they were driving the Mercedes-Benz G-Class southbound and making a right turn at approximately 9:40 PM.

The claimant recalls that it had been raining earlier and that the pavement was wet. They say they were driving "around 25 to 30 mph" before beginning the turn.

According to the claimant, the turn was normal until the vehicle suddenly slid. The claimant says they tried to correct the vehicle but the front of the Mercedes contacted a parked SUV.

The claimant says they did not see anyone inside the parked SUV and did not believe anyone was injured.

The claimant says they stopped after the collision, looked at the vehicles, and then left because they were concerned about being stranded late at night. They say they intended to report the incident.

The claimant does not recall the exact distance traveled, whether traction control activated, whether another vehicle was nearby, whether there was a witness, or the exact impact location.
